newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lac de Gras diamond sale plan late 1997 - BHP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lac de Gras diamond sale plan late 1997 - BHP.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd has pushed out to the fourth quarter of calendar 1997 a decision on how it will market diamonds from the C$1.1 billion Lac de Gras mine in Canada's Arctic.
"(A decision) will be during the fourth quarter. It wouldn't be before then," a BHP spokesman told Reuters.
BHP Diamonds president Jim Rothwell said in a recent speech to a Canadian mining conference: "BHP expects to conclude our deliberations and decide on a marketing strategy in the latter part of 1997."
In January, 29 percent joint venture partner Dia Met Minerals Ltd said the sales plan, which might include selling outside of the De Beers diamond cartel, would be finalised mid-year.
The BHP spokesman declined to comment on whether the sales plan would include De Beers' Central Selling Organisation but said discussions with all parties were continuing.
Rothwell's speech said that in developing the marketing plan BHP, which holds 51 percent of Lac de Gras, would have to ensure compliance with anti-competition laws in Canada and elsewhere.
The London-based CSO controls about 75 percent of world trade in uncut diamonds, selling to select traders and maintaining massive stockpiles.
Lac de Gras is expected to begin production in late 1998.
